scope: Theorem 5.10 (Universal plane covariance) of the manuscript “The Gaussian free field limit of integer Lipschitz heights with two-arc boundary data” (preprints/The-Gaussian-free-field-limit-of-integer-Lipschitz-heights-with-two-arc-boundary-data-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f0047faf78711628), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 30-31. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The rescaled spectral measures converge vaguely on the punctured plane to c∗ dp/|p|2, with 0 < c∗ < ∞. Put v = (2π)2c∗. For real f, g ∈ C∞ c (R2) of 30 integral zero, lim δ↓0 E[Hδ(f)Hδ(g)] = c∗ ∫ R2 ̂ f(ζ)̂ g(ζ) |ζ|2 dζ = v 2π ∫∫ R2×R2 f(x) log 1 |x − y| g(y) dx dy. (5.16) The same conclusion holds for tests converging in C∞ c with support in a common compact set.
